mxCell.value: Linear search: look at every item from left to right

function linearSearch(arr, target) {
  for (let i = 0; i < arr.length; i++) {
    if (arr[i] === target) return i;
  }
  return -1;
}

Any order works (no sorting)
Best case: first item, 1 check
Worst case: missing, n checks
O(n) time · O(1) memory
Built-ins that do a linear search: indexOf · includes · find · findIndex · some
Binary search: compare with the middle, drop half every round
blue = still possible · yellow = middle being compared · gray = dropped

function binarySearch(arr, target) {
  let left = 0;
  let right = arr.length - 1;
  while (left <= right) {
    const mid = left + Math.floor((right - left) / 2);
    if (arr[mid] === target) return mid;
    if (arr[mid] < target) left = mid + 1;
    else right = mid - 1;
  }
  return -1;
}
Both ends are included. right is the last index, not length.
<= because a range with one item (left === right) must still be checked.
Middle index. Same as floor((left + right) / 2) but never overflows.
Middle is too small → target can only be on the right of mid.
Middle is too big → target can only be on the left of mid.
left > right: the range is empty, so target is not there.
Every round either returns or makes the range smaller, so the loop always ends.
Why binary search is O(log n)
Doubling the data adds only one more round.

function lowerBound(nums, target) {
  let left = 0, right = nums.length;
  while (left < right) {
    const mid = left + Math.floor((right - left) / 2);
    if (nums[mid] < target) left = mid + 1;
    else right = mid;
  }
  return left;
}

Half-open range [left, right)
• right starts at length
• loop while (left < right)
• right = mid (mid may be it)
• upperBound: use <= not <
